## Setup

```{r}
# Load tidyverse: dplyr (data wrangling), stringr (text/regex), purrr (map),
# readr (read/write files), ggplot2 (plots), tibble, tidyr
library(tidyverse)

# Make every ggplot use a clean, minimal look
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
```

## 1. Read the transcripts

One `.txt` file per testimony in a `Testimonies/` folder. The file name (minus extension) becomes `person_id`.

```{r}
# List every file path inside the Testimonies folder
files <- list.files("Testimonies", full.names = TRUE)

# Drop anything that is a sub-folder rather than a file
files <- files[!dir.exists(files)]

testimonies <- tibble(
  # person_id = file name without the folder or ".txt"; str_trim removes stray spaces
  person_id = str_trim(tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(files))),
  # text = the full contents of each file, as one long string per person
  text      = map_chr(files, read_file)
) |>
  mutate(
    # Collapse all line breaks / repeated spaces into single spaces so regexes
    # can match phrases that were split across lines in the transcript
    text_clean = str_replace_all(text, "\\s+", " "),
    # Rough length of each transcript in words
    word_count = str_count(text_clean, "\\w+")
  )

# How many testimonies were loaded? (should be ~101)
nrow(testimonies)
```

## 2. Keyword dictionaries

Each entry is a regex (a text pattern). `|` means "or". Everything is matched case-insensitively. These are first drafts: expect to edit them after the validation step below.

```{r}
# ---- Destination countries -------------------------------------------------
# Name on the left = short label that ends up in the data.
# Text on the right = the words that count as a mention of that country.
destinations <- c(
  # "(?<!South |Latin |...)America" means: the word America, but NOT when it
  # follows "South ", "Latin ", "Central " or "North "
  us           = "United States|U\\.S\\.|the States|(?<!South |Latin |Central |North )America\\b",
  israel       = "Israel|Palestine",
  canada       = "Canada",
  australia    = "Australia",
  argentina    = "Argentina",
  brazil       = "Brazil",
  venezuela    = "Venezuela",
  uk           = "England|Britain|United Kingdom",
  france       = "France",
  sweden       = "Sweden",
  south_africa = "South Africa"
)

# ---- Movement language -----------------------------------------------------
# Words people use to describe going somewhere. Survivors rarely say
# "I emigrated"; they say "we went to", "I left Poland for", "we moved to".
# \\b = word boundary, so "go" does not match inside "good".
move_phrase <- paste0(
  "(emigrat\\w*|immigrat\\w*|\\bmov(e|ed|ing)\\b|\\bwent\\b|\\bgo(ing)?\\b|",
  "\\bgone\\b|\\bcame\\b|\\bcom(e|ing)\\b|sail\\w*|arriv\\w*|travel\\w*|",
  "\\bleft\\b|\\bleav(e|ing)\\b|settl\\w*|ended up|relocat\\w*|\\bfled\\b|\\bflew\\b)"
)

# ---- Other dictionaries ----------------------------------------------------
# One list holding five groups of keywords. Each group becomes a set of
# count columns (e.g. policy_visa = how many times "visa" appears).
dictionaries <- list(
  # Where the person was after the war
  situation = c(
    dp_camp    = "displaced persons|DP camp|D\\.P\\.|F(ö|oe)hrenwald|Landsberg|Feldafing|Zeilsheim|Pocking|Deggendorf|Ebelsberg",
    hiding     = "\\bhid\\b|hiding|hidden",
    liberation = "liberat"
  ),
  # Aid organizations
  org = c(
    hias          = "\\bHIAS\\b",
    jdc           = "\\bthe Joint\\b|\\bJDC\\b|Joint Distribution",
    iro           = "\\bIRO\\b|International Refugee Organization",
    unrra         = "\\bUNRRA\\b",
    jewish_agency = "Jewish Agency",
    red_cross     = "Red Cross"
  ),
  # Immigration policy mechanisms
  policy = c(
    quota       = "\\bquota",
    visa        = "\\bvisas?\\b",
    affidavit   = "affidavit",
    sponsor     = "sponsor",
    certificate = "certificate",
    dp_act      = "Displaced Persons Act",
    consulate   = "consulate|immigration (law|office|policy|restriction)"
  ),
  # Language about continued threat / fear
  threat = c(
    fear         = "afraid|fear|scared|terrif",
    pogrom       = "pogrom|Kielce",
    unsafe       = "not safe|unsafe|danger",
    antisemitism = "anti-?semit|hatred"
  ),
  # Language about making a decision to leave
  decision = c(
    decided   = "we decided|I decided|decided to",
    no_choice = "no choice|had to leave|couldn't stay|could not stay",
    waited    = "waited|waiting",
    wanted    = "wanted to leave|wanted to go|we chose|I chose"
  )
)

# Safety check: stop with a clear message if the list above didn't load properly
stopifnot(is.list(dictionaries), all(c("situation", "org", "policy", "threat", "decision") %in% names(dictionaries)))
```

## 3. Extract variables

```{r}
# ---- Helper 1: count_dict ---------------------------------------------------
# For every pattern in a dictionary, count how many times it appears in each
# transcript. Returns one column per pattern, named "<prefix>_<pattern name>".
count_dict <- function(text, dict, prefix) {
  map(dict, \(p) str_count(text, regex(p, ignore_case = TRUE))) |>  # count matches per pattern
    as_tibble() |>                                                   # list -> table
    rename_with(\(x) paste0(prefix, "_", x))                         # add prefix to column names
}

# ---- Helper 2: top_label ----------------------------------------------------
# Given a table of counts (rows = people, columns = categories), return the
# name of the column with the largest count for each person.
# If every count is 0, return NA (no match).
top_label <- function(df) {
  m <- as.matrix(df)
  ifelse(rowSums(m) == 0, NA_character_, colnames(m)[max.col(m, ties.method = "first")])
}

# ---- Destination ------------------------------------------------------------
# (a) Any mention of each country, anywhere in the text. Columns: mention_us, ...
dest_any <- count_dict(testimonies$text_clean, destinations, "mention")

# (b) A country mentioned within 80 characters AFTER a movement word.
#     Catches "we went to Canada", "I left Poland for Argentina", "moved to the States".
#     ".{0,80}?" = up to 80 of any characters, as few as possible.
dest_move <- map(destinations, \(p) {
  str_count(testimonies$text_clean,
            regex(paste0(move_phrase, ".{0,80}?(", p, ")"), ignore_case = TRUE))
}) |> as_tibble()

# Best guess #1: country with the most movement-phrase matches
dest_moved    <- top_label(dest_move)

# Best guess #2 (fallback): most-mentioned country overall, with "mention_" removed
dest_fallback <- top_label(dest_any) |> str_remove("^mention_")

# ---- Years ------------------------------------------------------------------
# A post-war year = 1945 to 1955.  19(4[5-9]|5[0-5]) means 194[5-9] or 195[0-5].
postwar_year <- "\\b(19(4[5-9]|5[0-5]))\\b"

# Departure word, then up to 80 characters in the same sentence, then a post-war year.
# Catches "we emigrated to the U.S. in 1949."
departure_re <- "(emigrat\\w*|immigrat\\w*|left|went|moved|sailed|arrived|came to|leave)[^.?!]{0,80}?\\b(19(4[5-9]|5[0-5]))\\b"

# Same idea, year first: "In 1949 we left for America."
departure_re_before <- "\\b(19(4[5-9]|5[0-5]))\\b[^.?!]{0,60}?(emigrat\\w*|immigrat\\w*|left|went|moved|sailed|leave)"

# For each transcript: every distinct post-war year mentioned, as whole numbers
years_all <- str_extract_all(testimonies$text_clean, postwar_year) |>
  map(\(y) as.integer(unique(y)))

# ---- Post-war situation patterns (used in the case_when below) ---------------
dp_camp_re <- dictionaries$situation[["dp_camp"]]
hiding_re  <- dictionaries$situation[["hiding"]]

# ---- Build the final dataset ------------------------------------------------
testimony_data <- testimonies |>
  # Attach all the keyword-count columns side by side
  bind_cols(
    count_dict(testimonies$text_clean, dictionaries$situation, "sit"),
    count_dict(testimonies$text_clean, dictionaries$org,       "org"),
    count_dict(testimonies$text_clean, dictionaries$policy,    "policy"),
    count_dict(testimonies$text_clean, dictionaries$threat,    "threat"),
    count_dict(testimonies$text_clean, dictionaries$decision,  "decision"),
    dest_any
  ) |>
  mutate(
    # Destination: movement-phrase match first; otherwise most-mentioned country
    destination = coalesce(dest_moved, dest_fallback),

    # Which method produced the destination (filter on this to be strict)
    destination_source = case_when(
      !is.na(dest_moved)    ~ "movement phrase",
      !is.na(dest_fallback) ~ "most mentioned",
      TRUE                  ~ NA_character_
    ),

    # Earliest and latest post-war year mentioned (NA if none)
    first_postwar_yr = map_int(years_all, \(y) if (length(y)) min(y) else NA_integer_),
    last_postwar_yr  = map_int(years_all, \(y) if (length(y)) max(y) else NA_integer_),

    # Departure year: try "departure word ... year", else "year ... departure word"
    # str_match(...)[, 3] pulls the year out of the 3rd bracket group of the first
    # pattern; [, 2] the 2nd bracket group of the second pattern
    departure_year = coalesce(
      as.integer(str_match(text_clean, regex(departure_re, ignore_case = TRUE))[, 3]),
      as.integer(str_match(text_clean, regex(departure_re_before, ignore_case = TRUE))[, 2])
    ),

    # Post-war situation: DP camp words first, then hiding words, else unclear
    post_war_situation = case_when(
      str_detect(text_clean, regex(dp_camp_re, ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "DP camp",
      str_detect(text_clean, regex(hiding_re,  ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Hiding / other",
      TRUE                                                          ~ "Unclear"
    ),

    # Total threat words, and threat words per 1,000 words (adjusts for length)
    threat_total   = rowSums(pick(starts_with("threat_"))),
    threat_per_1k  = threat_total / word_count * 1000,

    # Total decision-language words
    decision_total = rowSums(pick(starts_with("decision_"))),

    # TRUE if the person mentions any policy term / any aid organization
    any_policy     = rowSums(pick(starts_with("policy_"))) > 0,
    any_org        = rowSums(pick(starts_with("org_"))) > 0
  )

# Quick look at the key columns
glimpse(select(testimony_data, person_id, destination, destination_source,
               departure_year, post_war_situation, threat_per_1k, any_policy, any_org))

# How many destinations came from each method?
testimony_data |> count(destination, destination_source)
```

## 4. Validate before you trust it

The key step. Pick 5-10 testimonies, read the matches in context, and fix the regexes. `kwic()` shows each match with surrounding text.

```{r}
# kwic = "key word in context": prints each match with `width` characters of
# surrounding text on each side, for one person
kwic <- function(id, pattern, width = 80) {
  txt <- testimonies$text_clean[testimonies$person_id == id]   # that person's text
  str_extract_all(txt, regex(paste0(".{0,", width, "}(", pattern, ").{0,", width, "}"),
                             ignore_case = TRUE))[[1]]
}

# Examples (remove the # and swap in a real person_id and any pattern):
# kwic(testimonies$person_id[1], destinations[["us"]])
# kwic(testimonies$person_id[1], paste0(move_phrase, ".{0,80}?(", destinations[["us"]], ")"))
# kwic(testimonies$person_id[1], departure_re)
# kwic(testimonies$person_id[1], dictionaries$policy[["visa"]])
```

## 5. Add metadata and save

Expects `testimony_index.csv` with `person_id` (matching the file name exactly), `birth_year`, `birthplace`, `interview_date`.

```{r}
# Only merge metadata if you have made the index file
if (file.exists("testimony_index.csv")) {
  index <- read_csv("testimony_index.csv") |>
    mutate(person_id = str_trim(person_id))     # remove stray spaces so IDs match
  testimony_data <- left_join(testimony_data, index, by = "person_id")
}

# Save the dataset WITHOUT the full transcript text (keeps the file small and
# keeps survivors' words out of any shared file)
testimony_data |>
  select(-text, -text_clean) |>
  write_csv("testimony_data.csv")
```

## 6. First visualizations

```{r}
#| label: fig-destinations
# Bar chart: number of testimonies per destination country
testimony_data |>
  filter(!is.na(destination)) |>              # drop people with no destination found
  count(destination) |>                       # count rows per destination
  ggplot(aes(n, reorder(destination, n))) +   # sort bars by size
  geom_col(fill = "#2C5282") +
  labs(title = "Where survivors say they went",
       x = "Number of testimonies", y = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-situation
# Bar chart: DP camp vs hiding vs unclear
testimony_data |>
  count(post_war_situation) |>
  ggplot(aes(n, reorder(post_war_situation, n))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2C5282") +
  labs(title = "Post-war situation described", x = "Number of testimonies", y = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-departures
# Timeline: how many testimonies report leaving in each year
testimony_data |>
  filter(!is.na(departure_year)) |>
  count(departure_year) |>
  ggplot(aes(departure_year, n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2C5282") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1948, linetype = "dashed") +     # dashed line at 1948
  annotate("text", x = 1948.3, y = Inf, vjust = 1.5, hjust = 0, size = 3.5,
           label = "1948: U.S. DP Act /\nIsraeli independence") +
  labs(title = "Reported departure year", x = NULL, y = "Number of testimonies")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-policy
# Share of testimonies that mention each policy mechanism at least once
testimony_data |>
  summarise(across(starts_with("policy_"), \(x) mean(x > 0))) |>   # fraction with count > 0
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "mechanism", values_to = "share") |>
  mutate(mechanism = str_remove(mechanism, "policy_")) |>          # tidy labels
  ggplot(aes(share, reorder(mechanism, share))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2C5282") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(title = "Share of testimonies mentioning each policy mechanism",
       x = "Share of testimonies", y = NULL)
```
